title: _emergencyWithdraw bypasses the documented 24h rugpull delay AND leaves clientBalances/totalDeposited untouched, producing both a one-tx drain path and permanent accounting skew

classification.assetImpact: Once the owner triggers an emergency withdraw (even legitimately), clientBalances and totalDeposited are not decremented. Subsequent legitimate withdrawals compute against stale state and revert or return wrong amounts, breaking protocol availability for honest clients.
attackPath: 1. Owner calls _emergencyWithdraw to remove funds for any (legitimate or otherwise) reason.
2. The function transfers shares out but leaves clientBalances[token][client] and totalDeposited[token] unchanged.

3. After the call, totalShares << totalDeposited * clientBalances accounting; any client withdrawal computes sharesToWithdraw against stale totalDeposited, returning incorrect amounts or reverting because availableShares is exhausted.
4. Even an honest emergency-then-restore flow leaves the strategy permanently mis-accounted unless the owner manually re-bookkeeps.
classification.likelihood: medium - requires owner to invoke emergency withdraw, but this is an intended operational path

justification: Protocol function/availability is impacted whenever the (intended) emergency-withdraw path is exercised, due to missing accounting decrements. The rugpull-delay-bypass framing alone would be Centralization, but the accounting-skew bug makes this Medium because honest use of the intended emergency path produces broken state for clients afterward.
